purpose: Continue post-coverage multiplicity sampling across 67500, 67930, 76597, 77967 and 95324 with privacy/security, civil standards, dependency hygiene, software-security research, AI workflow, filesystem-boundary and connector-standard sources.

policy.rule: After 208/208 baseline coverage, additional occurrences are accumulated by independent namespace and utility domain with zero automatic physical-evidence weight.
policy.promotion: New CVEs, issue numbers, theses, article IDs, bug numbers and standards remain M1/N0 unless the digits independently encode a verified physical quantity; physical promotion is unchanged.
policy.historical: Prior NO_HIT observations remain valid descriptions of earlier search passes and are not deleted when later sources are found.

Illumination of lock areas — requirements, design and measurement; replaces/updates a long-running civil/maritime lighting standard lineage

information_updates.finding: CVE-2025-67500 adds an information-leakage class based on response-shape discrepancies rather than content disclosure, useful for testing whether authorization failures reveal object existence through localization/status-code/error differences.
information_updates.claims_boundary: 67500 is the CVE identifier and DIN standard number in separate namespaces.

information_updates.finding: DIN 67500 expands maritime/civil test coverage to engineered illumination of lock areas, bringing lighting requirements, calculations and measurement into the environmental/civil corpus.
information_updates.claims_boundary: The shared digits with CVE-2025-67500 are an unrelated namespace collision.

information_updates.finding: The AI-reporting study demonstrates a deployment lesson important beyond medicine: an AI tool can initially increase task time during adaptation and show delayed productivity benefit, so Worldshepherd AI evaluations should model learning curves rather than measuring only immediate post-deployment throughput.
VG 95324 provides current connector-design standards relevant to printed-board hardware qualification and supply-chain part/specification mapping.

next_actions: Continue post-coverage multiplicity sampling and identify states with only one namespace so collision-frequency estimates become less dominated by densely indexed identifiers.
Use the accumulated AI deployment/adaptation literature to add learning-curve and operator-adoption metrics to future Worldshepherd AI validation plans.
Continue same-system topology and relational verification independently for physical P1/P2 candidates.
